← Harness Lab

Conformance remediation 5.3

29 October 2026 • All 97 assessment entries mapped.

The assessment audited V5.1 definitions. This release adds explicit operating controls and local reference tests to the current V5.2 methods. Historical grades below are unchanged. Documented controls do not prove a host implements them.

Priority fixes cover turn, cost and deadline limits; replayable traces; isolation; compaction; machine-readable policy; skill trust; secret redaction; model conditioning; lifecycle hooks; and usage reporting. Missing required host enforcement blocks the affected stage.

Original assessment · Implementation and acceptance guide · 97-entry traceability matrix · Updated complete release

Controls, evidence and remaining host verification

REQ-LOOP-01 — Partially meets

Explicit action-observation loop

Use a linear inference → validate → authorize → execute → append observation loop. Append every tool result before the next inference; gate completion independently.

Status: Specified; host integration acceptance required

REQ-LOOP-02 — Partially meets

Start as a linear loop. A middleware- pipeline architecture shall be adopted only when three or more independent turn-level policies must coexist…

Keep the linear baseline. Introduce middleware only after documenting at least three independent turn policies and their ordering; denial is final.

Status: Specified; host integration acceptance required

REQ-LOOP-03 — Partially meets

Enforce hard caps on turns and on cost (or tokens), checked every turn, and shall terminate with a recorded reason when a cap is reached. The…

Before every turn and dispatch reserve token/cost allowance; enforce max_turns, max_tokens and max_cost_usd including children and retries. Stop before overspend; unknown usage blocks paid dispatch. Persist termination_reason.

Status: Specified; host integration acceptance required

REQ-LOOP-04 — Does not meet

Cap consecutive malformed or format- error model responses and shall enforce a wall-clock limit, as minimum stuck protection. More elaborate stuck…

Enforce stage deadline and per-call cancellation timeout; default 3 consecutive malformed responses, 30 turns, 900 seconds. Reset format-error streak only after schema-valid response. A supervisor must cancel hung calls.

Status: Specified; host integration acceptance required

REQ-LOOP-05 — Unverified

Tool calls from a single model response should be executed as a batch. Where parallel execution is offered, calls that touch the same declared…

Batch independent reads; serialize calls sharing a declared writable resource. Keep observation order in call-ID order; dependent operations stay sequential.

Status: Specified; host integration acceptance required

REQ-LOOP-06 — Partially meets

Be returned to the model as observations (with exception type and message), not raised as harness crashes, so the loop can recover within the turn…

Return errors as observations with call_id, exception_type, redacted message and retryable flag. Bound retries within all original limits; never fabricate success.

Status: Specified; host integration acceptance required

REQ-LOOP-07 — Exceeds

Reflection and repair

Preserve the existing generate/validate/critique/repair procedure and independent review.

Status: Preserved and clarified

REQ-LOOP-08 — Exceeds

Where a completion claim must be trusted, the harness should support an outer verification step — a judge, critic, test run, or verify-on- stop…

Require the independent Ground Truth Gatekeeper before stage promotion; the author cannot be the sole approver.

Status: Preserved and clarified

REQ-LOOP-09 — Partially meets

Record a complete, replayable trace of each run: prompts or prompt references, model responses, tool calls, observations, and termination reason.…

Persist RunTrace/v1 with input/prompt references, normalized responses, ordered calls, observations, compaction, permission rule IDs, timing, usage and termination. Replay uses recorded responses, never repeats external side effects.

Status: Specified; host integration acceptance required

REQ-LOOP-10 — Unverified

Be surfaced incrementally to the interface layer where the deployment is interactive, without changing loop semantics.

Interactive adapters may emit ordered text/tool/progress events; accumulate the same final normalized response as nonstreaming. Disconnect does not authorize repeated actions.

Status: Specified; host integration acceptance required

REQ-LLM-01 — Partially meets

Isolate all provider communication behind a single model interface (a complete(messages, tools) style seam or equivalent), so the loop, tools, and…

Use one complete(messages, tools, limits) interface returning text, tool_calls with stable IDs, finish_reason and usage; provider wire formats stay inside adapters.

Status: Specified; host integration acceptance required

REQ-LLM-02 — Partially meets

If the harness ships with its own foundation model, it shall couple tightly to the home provider and shall expose a generic fallback adapter for…

No foundation model ships here. Use generic normalized adapter with explicit capability negotiation; reject unsupported features instead of silently weakening controls.

REQ-LLM-03 — Does not meet

The conditioning layer should carry, per model or provider as applicable: cache- breakpoint placement and dialect, thinking / reasoning-effort…

Status: Specified; host integration acceptance required

REQ-LLM-04 — Does not meet

Be structured for caching: a stable static prefix, cache boundaries at stable split points, and no per-turn mutation of the cached prefix.…

Freeze static instructions and tool catalogue prefix per run; append changing state after a stable cache boundary. Report cached/uncached tokens separately when available; never invent cache savings.

Status: Specified; host integration acceptance required

REQ-LLM-05 — Unverified

Route requests between model variants (for example cheapest-sufficient routing, or a weaker cheaper model for summarisation) provided routing…

Model routing is opt-in. Record chosen model, reason and quality evidence; default to operator-selected model. Cheaper summaries still pass evidence and retention checks.

Where prompt content differs by model family or generation, the variants should be managed as an explicit matrix or gated blocks with the observed…

Status: Specified; host integration acceptance required

REQ-LLM-09 — Unverified

Normalise provider event streams into the loop’s single response representation, preserving tool-call identity so observations can be matched to…

Normalize provider streaming deltas into text, tool-call IDs and arguments; reject duplicate or orphan IDs. Validate completed arguments before permission evaluation.

Status: Specified; host integration acceptance required

REQ-LLM-10 — Unverified

A multi-provider harness may emit multiple providers’ cache dialects simultaneously, or normalise prefixes for local inference backends, where…

REQ-TOOL-03 — Unverified

When the exposed tool count exceeds approximately 15, the harness shall adopt deferred tool loading: most schemas leave the initial prompt, and…

REQ-TOOL-04 — Does not meet

Tool results shall be truncated to a bounded size before entering the context, and shell- tool results shall include exit status and both output…

Status: Specified; host integration acceptance required

REQ-TOOL-05 — Unverified

Be matched to the model tier: exact unique-substring replacement for frontier models; a fuzzy matching cascade, indentation-aware matching, or…

Status: Specified; host integration acceptance required

REQ-TOOL-06 — Unverified

No edit tool shall address content by line number as its primary contract. Drift between the model’s view and the file’s current state shall be…

Status: Specified; host integration acceptance required

REQ-TOOL-07 — Partially meets

Be provided through deterministic tools — ripgrep-backed search, glob, filesystem traversal, and tree-sitter symbol extraction where a repository…

Status: Specified; host integration acceptance required

Not wrap every upstream SaaS or product API as a one-to-one tool. Related operations shall be consolidated into task-level tools shaped for the…

REQ-TOOL-10 — Partially meets

Each tool should declare the resources it touches (files, terminal, browser, network) so the loop can apply the concurrency rules of REQ-LOOP-05…

Execute tool calls as code in an embedded runtime, or batch independent calls, where the deployment justifies it. These are Maximal options, not…

REQ-CTX-01 — Partially meets

Hierarchical context discovery

REQ-CTX-02 — Partially meets

Be injected near the top of the system prompt. Nested context files should be surfaced just-in- time, when a tool touches their subtree, rather…

Implement threshold compaction: it fires at a fixed buffer below the model’s effective context window, preserves a verbatim recent tail, and…

Merge each new summary into the previous summary incrementally (anchored / iterative summarisation), preserving early decisions that from-scratch…

REQ-CTX-05 — Unverified

Use unbounded linear history, provided turn and cost caps (REQ- LOOP-03) bound the run and the limitation is documented. Linear history shall not…

REQ-SAFE-07 — Unverified

REQ-SAFE-09 — Partially meets

Not present a partial in- process sandbox as a security boundary. Either execution is isolated by an operating- system mechanism (or a delegated…
